Terms of use

The agreement between you and Quota, and the community guidelines that are part of it.

Last updated 2026-11-02

These terms are the agreement between you and Quota, which is run by its two co-founders, Ari Marants and Justin Smith (“Quota”, “we”). By creating an account or using the app you agree to them, to the community guidelines, and to the privacy policy. If you do not agree, do not use Quota.

No tolerance for objectionable content or abusive users

There is no tolerance on Quota for objectionable content or for abusive behaviour. That means harassment, bullying, hate speech, threats, sexual content, content involving anybody under 18 in any sexual way, and anything else the community guidelines rule out. Posting it, or treating people that way, gets the content removed and the account suspended or deleted, with no warning required.

  • Every post, story, comment, message and profile can be reported from inside the app, and anybody can be blocked.
  • Reports are reviewed within 24 hours. Content that breaks these terms is removed, and the account behind it is removed as well where the guidelines say so.
  • Whoever made a group can remove any post from it.

Your account

  • You must be 13 or older.
  • Give a real email address and keep your password to yourself. You are responsible for what happens on your account.
  • One person, one account. Do not make an account to get around a block or a removal.
  • You can delete your account at any time from Settings. It deletes everything in it.

What you post

You own what you post. By posting it you give Quota permission to store it and show it to the people you shared it with, which is only what the app needs to work, and that permission ends when you delete it. Post only what you have the right to post, and only film people who are happy to be filmed.

You are responsible for what you post, and for what you agree to with your groups, forfeits included. Quota does not review posts before they go up, and a forfeit is between the people in a group: Quota does not set it, enforce it, or answer for it.

Using Quota fairly

Do not try to break, overload, or get around the app or its security; do not scrape it or read other people's data; and do not use it for anything illegal.

If things go wrong

Quota is free and is provided as it is. We work to keep it running and your data safe, but we cannot promise it will never be unavailable or lose something. As far as the law allows, we are not liable for indirect losses, or for what other people post. Nothing here takes away rights you have under the law where you live.

Ending it

You can stop using Quota and delete your account whenever you like. We can suspend or remove an account that breaks these terms, and we may change or stop the app. If these terms change in a way that matters you will be asked to agree again before carrying on.

The app stores

If you got Quota from Apple's App Store, these terms are between you and Quota, not Apple, and Apple has no responsibility for the app or its content. Apple's standard licence terms for apps also apply, and Apple and its subsidiaries may enforce these terms as third-party beneficiaries.

Community guidelines

Quota is for showing your friends you did the thing. Everything below follows from that.

The proof is yours, and it is real

  • Post your own effort, filmed by you. Not a clip from last year, not somebody else's, not something off the internet.
  • Say the number you actually did. A group only works if the number means something.
  • Film other people only if they are happy to be filmed.

How people are treated

  • No harassment, no pile-ons, no going after somebody for missing a day. Pressure is the point of the app. Cruelty is not.
  • No slurs and no hate — about race, religion, nationality, disability, sex, gender or sexuality. This is the line there is no version of.
  • No threats of violence, and nothing encouraging anybody to hurt themselves.
  • No posting somebody else's private information.
  • No pretending to be someone you are not, in a username, a display name or anywhere else.

Forfeits

A forfeit is a small, friendly price for a missed day. Keep it that way.

  • Cheap, safe and fun: buying the coffee, extra pushups, planning the next hangout.
  • Nothing dangerous, nothing involving alcohol or drugs, nothing sexual, and nothing meant to humiliate somebody. A little friendly embarrassing is fine; cruelty is not.
  • Never money, and nothing anybody has not agreed to by joining the group.

Nobody has to do a forfeit that breaks these rules, and whoever set it can be reported from their profile like anything else.

What does not go on Quota

  • Nudity and sexual content.
  • Illegal activity, or anything encouraging it.
  • Spam, scams, and accounts set up to advertise something.
  • Anything you do not have the right to post.

Language

Quota checks what you type before it saves it. Slurs, sexually explicit words and strong swearing are refused in captions, comments, stories, group names, bios and usernames, and you are told which word stopped it and why. It is a word list, not a reading of what you meant — take the word out and the rest goes through.

The list is not exhaustive. Getting something past it does not make it allowed; the rest of this page still applies.

Age

You have to be 13 or older to use Quota.

If these are broken

Posts, comments and stories that break these guidelines are taken down. An account that keeps breaking them is removed, and for slurs, threats, or sexual content involving anybody under 18 it goes on the first time.

Reporting and blocking

Tap ⋯ on a post or a story, or press and hold a comment or a message, and choose Report. Report and Block are also on everybody's profile. Every report is looked at within 24 hours. Blocking somebody hides everything they make from you straight away, and they are not told. You can also email hello@hitquota.app.
